newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst chief - no plans to quit German base.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst chief - no plans to quit German base.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG fresh from announcing plans to overhaul its corporate structure, on Thursday said it would not leave Germany as long as conditions here do not deteriorate.
Hoechst last month announced plans to transform itself into a strategic management holding group leaving its various business units as separate entities.
The move, part of a bid to cut costs and boost shareholder value, raised speculation that Hoechst may abandon Germany altogether, moving its headquarters abroad to take advantage of lower costs.
In an interview with the weekly German newspaper Die Zeit, Hoechst management board chairman Juergen Dormann however shrugged off suggestions of a move.
"We know the roots of this company. If Germany shows an ability to regenerate itself and makes up ground in innovation, then there will be no need to leave this site," Dormann told the newspaper.
Dormann also said that he expects the wave of job cuts which flooded the chemicals industry as companies scrambled to modernise during the recession is largely over.
"I personally think that the wave of job cuts in Germany has largely been completed," Dormann said.
Several chemicals groups have said that Germany's high costs, including the high tax rate and wage costs as well as crusty bureaucracies, have prompted them to move some production abroad.
